tests.name: 1. The read
tests.setting: A 10-minute conversation with a trusted friend, a colleague you trust, or Claude role-playing a counterpart with a hidden need
tests.pass: Baseline noted in the first minute. Conversation type named. One need hypothesis written, then checked back in the conversation and confirmed or corrected. At least one label followed by a full pause.

tests.name: 2. Office dojo, live
tests.setting: One real work conversation where someone holds a position that blocks you
tests.pass: You name or answer the concern under the position before you argue your own. You check back at least once. Your own ask still made (White Belt rules hold).

tests.name: 3. Personal dojo, live
tests.pass: You go first with a ping, respect the answer, and, if the ping is returned, propose a specific next meeting yourself

starterCodex.context: High-pressure office crunch right before an unvetted scope handoff.
starterCodex.range: Appears across polished Achievers and covert pushers alike.
starterCodex.harm: Hooks your Intelligence/Approval need into saying yes against your own bandwidth.
starterCodex.remedy: “Thanks for saying that. I still can't take on Q3 reconciliation this week.”
starterCodex.ethical: Genuine, specific appreciation with zero strings or hidden ask attached.
starterCodex.temptation: Praising a colleague's expertise right before asking them to cover an awkward task.

starterCodex.context: Negotiations or vendor renewals demanding same-day sign-off without data review.
starterCodex.range: Common in sales, procurement, and anxious management chains.
starterCodex.harm: Bypasses deliberation and forces unilateral concessions.
starterCodex.remedy: “I notice we're being pushed to lock this before reviewing assumptions—I'll respond tomorrow at 10 AM.”
starterCodex.ethical: Sharing a real, transparent external cutoff early so both sides can plan.
starterCodex.temptation: Using 'deadline pressure' to close a debate when I feel impatient.

starterCodex.context: Verbal agreements revisited later with 'That's not what we agreed.'
starterCodex.range: Appears under budget stress or accountability avoidance.
starterCodex.harm: Erodes confidence in your own memory and extracts unpaid rework.
starterCodex.remedy: Point calmly to the 3-line confirming email; do not debate memory.
starterCodex.ethical: Explicitly flagging when new material facts require renegotiating an old agreement.
starterCodex.temptation: Rationalizing a missed personal commitment as 'we never locked a firm time.'
